display_name: Terra Australis, schematic envelope (not a digitised coastline)
notes: A latitude envelope standing for the region within which the conjectured continent was drawn. It is deliberately not a coastline: no map in the register has been examined, so there is nothing to digitise, and drawing a plausible outline would manufacture the very false precision the essay is about.

display_name: Coronelli's southern polar region, as treated in 1693
source_locator: Atlante Veneto, printed pp. 70 and 76; Rumsey 12186.101
notes: A non-spatial evidence record. The examined plate is Arctic to the neatline, while the accompanying text treats the far south and rejects several claimed lands as fabulous. The record carries no geometry because this is evidence of textual treatment and graphic absence, not a mappable southern extent.

display_name: Southern limit reached by Resolution, 30 January 1774
notes: The furthest south of the second voyage, commonly given as 71 degrees 10 minutes south, 106 degrees 54 minutes west. Recorded from the general literature and not yet checked against Beaglehole, which is why it stays raw.

The one pilot record whose identity is established from a catalogue record read directly, which is why it is the only row at normalized. Its later_status is modified rather than confirmed because the sheet is itself a reissue of an 1874 compilation.
